name: SSC Sentence Improvement and Error Correction
description: Mixed SSC sentence improvement and correction traps across grammar, usage, prepositions, redundancy, and word order.

cards.term: Error: The quality of these apples are good.
cards.definition:
Improved: The quality of these apples is good.

Rule: The true subject is quality, not apples.

Memory hook: Find the real subject before trusting the nearest noun.

cards.term: Error: The list of candidates have been published.
cards.definition:
Improved: The list of candidates has been published.

Rule: List is singular, so use has.

Memory hook: The list is one document, even if it contains many names.

cards.term: Error: Each of the students have submitted the form.
cards.definition:
Improved: Each of the students has submitted the form.

Rule: Each is singular.

Memory hook: Each behaves like one strict invigilator.

cards.term: Error: Neither of the two answers are correct.
cards.definition:
Improved: Neither of the two answers is correct.

Rule: Neither is singular when referring to two options.

Memory hook: Neither means not one, so keep it singular.

cards.term: Error: Either of these roads lead to the station.
cards.definition:
Improved: Either of these roads leads to the station.

Rule: Either is singular.

Memory hook: Either road may help, but grammar treats either as one.

cards.term: Error: A number of students has applied.
cards.definition:
Improved: A number of students have applied.

Rule: A number of means many and takes plural verb.

Memory hook: A number of students are a crowd, not one statistic.

cards.term: Error: The number of applicants are increasing.
cards.definition:
Improved: The number of applicants is increasing.

Rule: The number refers to one figure.

Memory hook: The number is one figure sitting on a chart.

cards.term: Error: Many a student have made this mistake.
cards.definition:
Improved: Many a student has made this mistake.

Rule: Many a takes singular noun and singular verb.

Memory hook: Many a looks plural in meaning but behaves singular in grammar.

cards.term: Error: More than one candidate have arrived.
cards.definition:
Improved: More than one candidate has arrived.

Rule: More than one usually takes singular verb.

Memory hook: This phrase means more than one, but exam grammar treats it as singular.

cards.term: Error: The news are shocking.
cards.definition:
Improved: The news is shocking.

Rule: News is singular despite ending in s.

Memory hook: News wears an s but behaves like a singular noun.

cards.term: Error: Mathematics are difficult for him.
cards.definition:
Improved: Mathematics is difficult for him.

Rule: Names of subjects ending in s are singular.

Memory hook: Subjects like mathematics are one field, not many objects.

cards.term: Error: The scissors is on the table.
cards.definition:
Improved: The scissors are on the table.

Rule: Scissors is treated as plural.

Memory hook: Two blades, plural behaviour.

cards.term: Error: A pair of scissors are missing.
cards.definition:
Improved: A pair of scissors is missing.

Rule: A pair is singular.

Memory hook: The pair is one unit, even if the scissors have two blades.

cards.term: Error: The police is investigating the case.
cards.definition:
Improved: The police are investigating the case.

Rule: Police is treated as plural.

Memory hook: Police means people in uniform, so use are.

cards.term: Error: The cattle is grazing.
cards.definition:
Improved: The cattle are grazing.

Rule: Cattle is plural.

Memory hook: Cattle never behaves like a single cow.

cards.term: Error: The committee have taken its decision.
cards.definition:
Improved: The committee has taken its decision.

Rule: A committee acting as one body takes singular verb.

Memory hook: If the group acts as one unit, use singular.

cards.term: Error: The committee has divided in their opinions.
cards.definition:
Improved: The committee have divided in their opinions.

Rule: When members act separately, collective noun may take plural verb.

Memory hook: When the group starts arguing internally, plural makes sense.

cards.term: Error: Bread and butter are my breakfast.
cards.definition:
Improved: Bread and butter is my breakfast.

Rule: One combined dish or idea takes singular verb.

Memory hook: Breakfast on one plate is one idea.

cards.term: Error: The poet and philosopher are dead.
cards.definition:
Improved: The poet and philosopher is dead.

Rule: If one person has both titles, use singular verb.

Memory hook: One person wearing two labels still needs one verb.

cards.term: Error: The poet and the philosopher is dead.
cards.definition:
Improved: The poet and the philosopher are dead.

Rule: Two different people take plural verb.

Memory hook: Two the's usually signal two people.

cards.term: Error: The principal and secretary have arrived.
cards.definition:
Improved: The principal and secretary has arrived.

Rule: One person holding both posts takes singular verb.

Memory hook: One chair, two nameplates.

cards.term: Error: The principal and the secretary has arrived.
cards.definition:
Improved: The principal and the secretary have arrived.

Rule: Two different people take plural verb.

Memory hook: Two the's, two people.

cards.term: Error: Neither the teacher nor the students is ready.
cards.definition:
Improved: Neither the teacher nor the students are ready.

Rule: With neither...nor, verb agrees with the nearer subject students.

Memory hook: The nearer subject controls the verb.

cards.term: Error: Neither the students nor the teacher are ready.
cards.definition:
Improved: Neither the students nor the teacher is ready.

Rule: Verb agrees with nearer subject teacher.

Memory hook: The verb obeys the neighbour beside it.

cards.term: Error: The captain, along with his players, are ready.
cards.definition:
Improved: The captain, along with his players, is ready.

Rule: Along with does not change the main subject.

Memory hook: Ignore the guest phrase and find the real subject.

cards.term: Error: The teacher as well as the students are excited.
cards.definition:
Improved: The teacher as well as the students is excited.

Rule: As well as does not make the subject plural.

Memory hook: As well as adds information, not verb power.

cards.term: Error: There is many reasons for failure.
cards.definition:
Improved: There are many reasons for failure.

Rule: Verb agrees with the real subject reasons after there.

Memory hook: There is not the subject, look after it.

cards.term: Error: Here is the documents you wanted.
cards.definition:
Improved: Here are the documents you wanted.

Rule: Documents is plural.

Memory hook: Here and there introduce the subject, they do not decide the verb.

cards.term: Error: One-third of the students is absent.
cards.definition:
Improved: One-third of the students are absent.

Rule: Fraction of plural noun takes plural verb.

Memory hook: One-third of people still means people.

cards.term: Error: One-third of the work are complete.
cards.definition:
Improved: One-third of the work is complete.

Rule: Fraction of uncountable work takes singular verb.

Memory hook: Work is a mass noun, so use is.

cards.term: Error: The data is reliable.
cards.definition:
Improved: The data are reliable.

Rule: In formal exam grammar, data is plural.

Memory hook: Data is the old plural of datum, even if modern usage is flexible.

cards.term: Error: The criteria is strict.
cards.definition:
Improved: The criteria are strict.

Rule: Criteria is plural, criterion is singular.

Memory hook: Criteria are many filters at the gate.

cards.term: Error: The furniture are expensive.
cards.definition:
Improved: The furniture is expensive.

Rule: Furniture is uncountable and singular in agreement.

Memory hook: Furniture is a mass category, not furnitures.

cards.term: Error: The information are useful.
cards.definition:
Improved: The information is useful.

Rule: Information is uncountable.

Memory hook: Information never becomes informations.

cards.term: Error: His means is limited.
cards.definition:
Improved: His means are limited.

Rule: Means meaning resources is often plural.

Memory hook: Resources come in plural pockets.

cards.term: Error: He has went to the market.
cards.definition:
Improved: He has gone to the market.

Rule: Use V3 after has, have, or had.

Memory hook: Has went is a classic trap, has gone is the safe answer.

cards.term: Error: She had saw the movie earlier.
cards.definition:
Improved: She had seen the movie earlier.

Rule: Had is followed by V3.

Memory hook: Had saw is like wearing two wrong shoes.

cards.term: Error: They have ate dinner.
cards.definition:
Improved: They have eaten dinner.

Rule: Present perfect needs have plus V3.

Memory hook: Have eaten is the grammar plate.

cards.term: Error: He did not went there.
cards.definition:
Improved: He did not go there.

Rule: Did not is followed by base verb.

Memory hook: Did already carries the past tense.

cards.term: Error: Did you saw him yesterday?
cards.definition:
Improved: Did you see him yesterday?

Rule: Did is followed by base verb.

Memory hook: After did, the main verb becomes simple again.

cards.term: Error: She does not likes coffee.
cards.definition:
Improved: She does not like coffee.

Rule: Does not is followed by base verb.

Memory hook: Does carries the s, so like does not need it.

cards.term: Error: He go to school daily.
cards.definition:
Improved: He goes to school daily.

Rule: Singular third person takes s/es in simple present.

Memory hook: He needs goes, they need go.

cards.term: Error: The boys goes to school daily.
cards.definition:
Improved: The boys go to school daily.

Rule: Plural subject takes base verb in simple present.

Memory hook: Boys are plural, so no extra s on go.

cards.term: Error: I am knowing the answer.
cards.definition:
Improved: I know the answer.

Rule: Stative verbs like know usually do not take continuous form.

Memory hook: You know an answer, you do not usually know-ing it.

cards.term: Error: She is having a car.
cards.definition:
Improved: She has a car.

Rule: Have meaning possession is not normally continuous.

Memory hook: Possession prefers has, not is having.

cards.term: Error: I am living here since 2020.
cards.definition:
Improved: I have been living here since 2020.

Rule: Use present perfect continuous for action continuing from past to present.

Memory hook: Since needs a bridge from past to now.

cards.term: Error: She is waiting for an hour.
cards.definition:
Improved: She has been waiting for an hour.

Rule: For plus duration continuing to present takes present perfect continuous.

Memory hook: If the waiting is still alive, use has been waiting.

cards.term: Error: I know him since childhood.
cards.definition:
Improved: I have known him since childhood.

Rule: Stative continuing state takes present perfect.

Memory hook: Known is the long-term version of know.

cards.term: Error: He has visited Delhi yesterday.
cards.definition:
Improved: He visited Delhi yesterday.

Rule: Use simple past with definite past time like yesterday.

Memory hook: Yesterday locks the action in the past.

cards.term: Error: She has called me last night.
cards.definition:
Improved: She called me last night.

Rule: Finished past time takes simple past.

Memory hook: Last night and present perfect do not sit together in SSC grammar.

cards.term: Error: I have met him two days ago.
cards.definition:
Improved: I met him two days ago.

Rule: Ago requires simple past.

Memory hook: Ago pushes the sentence firmly into the past.

cards.term: Error: When I reached, he left.
cards.definition:
Improved: When I reached, he had left.

Rule: Earlier of two past actions takes past perfect.

Memory hook: He left first, so he gets had left.

cards.term: Error: The train left before we reached.
cards.definition:
Improved: The train had left before we reached.

Rule: Use past perfect for the earlier past action.

Memory hook: The train escaped before you arrived.

cards.term: Error: I will call you when I will reach home.
cards.definition:
Improved: I will call you when I reach home.

Rule: Future time clauses use present tense after when.

Memory hook: When clause does not need another will.

cards.term: Error: If he will work hard, he will pass.
cards.definition:
Improved: If he works hard, he will pass.

Rule: First conditional uses if plus simple present.

Memory hook: If clause hates extra will.

cards.term: Error: Unless you will hurry, you will miss the train.
cards.definition:
Improved: Unless you hurry, you will miss the train.

Rule: Use present tense after unless for future meaning.

Memory hook: Unless behaves like if in future conditions.

cards.term: Error: I wish I am rich.
cards.definition:
Improved: I wish I were rich.

Rule: Wish for unreal present uses past subjunctive.

Memory hook: Wish creates an unreal world, so use were.

cards.term: Error: If I was you, I would apologise.
cards.definition:
Improved: If I were you, I would apologise.

Rule: Unreal condition commonly uses were.

Memory hook: If I were you is the exam-safe phrase.

cards.term: Error: If I would have known, I would have helped.
cards.definition:
Improved: If I had known, I would have helped.

Rule: Third conditional uses if plus had V3.

Memory hook: Never put would in the if-clause here.

cards.term: Error: It is time you go home.
cards.definition:
Improved: It is time you went home.

Rule: It is time is followed by past tense for present/future action.

Memory hook: High time and it is time push the verb into past form.

cards.term: Error: He talks as if he knows everything.
cards.definition:
Improved: He talks as if he knew everything.

Rule: Unreal comparison after as if takes past tense.

Memory hook: He does not know everything, so grammar signals unreality.

cards.term: Error: He made me to wait.
cards.definition:
Improved: He made me wait.

Rule: Make plus object takes bare infinitive.

Memory hook: Make someone do, not make someone to do.

cards.term: Error: Let him to go.
cards.definition:
Improved: Let him go.

Rule: Let plus object takes bare infinitive.

Memory hook: Let removes the to.

cards.term: Error: I heard him to sing.
cards.definition:
Improved: I heard him sing.

Rule: Verbs of perception take bare infinitive for complete action.

Memory hook: Hear someone sing, not hear someone to sing.

cards.term: Error: Avoid to make mistakes.
cards.definition:
Improved: Avoid making mistakes.

Rule: Avoid is followed by gerund.

Memory hook: Avoid plus -ing is the safe pair.

cards.term: Error: He denied to steal the money.
cards.definition:
Improved: He denied stealing the money.

Rule: Deny is followed by gerund.

Memory hook: Deny doing, not deny to do.

cards.term: Error: I look forward to meet you.
cards.definition:
Improved: I look forward to meeting you.

Rule: To in look forward to is a preposition, so use gerund.

Memory hook: This to behaves like a preposition, not an infinitive marker.

cards.term: Error: He insisted to go.
cards.definition:
Improved: He insisted on going.

Rule: Insist is followed by on plus gerund.

Memory hook: Insist on doing is the standard phrase.

cards.term: Error: She succeeded to pass the exam.
cards.definition:
Improved: She succeeded in passing the exam.

Rule: Succeed is followed by in plus gerund.

Memory hook: Success travels with in.

cards.term: Error: He is used to work hard.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is used to working hard.

Rule: Be used to takes gerund.

Memory hook: Accustomed-to grammar needs -ing.

cards.term: Error: I used to going there.
cards.definition:
Improved: I used to go there.

Rule: Used to for past habit takes base verb.

Memory hook: Past habit uses used to do.

cards.term: Error: He must goes now.
cards.definition:
Improved: He must go now.

Rule: Modals are followed by base verb.

Memory hook: After modal, verb becomes plain.

cards.term: Error: She can sings well.
cards.definition:
Improved: She can sing well.

Rule: Can takes base verb.

Memory hook: Can already has power, no s needed.

cards.term: Error: You ought work hard.
cards.definition:
Improved: You ought to work hard.

Rule: Ought is followed by to plus base verb.

Memory hook: Ought carries its own to.

cards.term: Error: He had better to leave.
cards.definition:
Improved: He had better leave.

Rule: Had better is followed by base verb.

Memory hook: Had better drops to.

cards.term: Error: She cannot able to solve it.
cards.definition:
Improved: She cannot solve it.

Rule: Do not use can and able to together like this.

Memory hook: Can and able to are two drivers for one car.

cards.term: Error: He is a honest man.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is an honest man.

Rule: Use an before vowel sound. Honest begins with silent h.

Memory hook: Listen to sound, not spelling.

cards.term: Error: She reached after a hour.
cards.definition:
Improved: She reached after an hour.

Rule: Hour begins with a vowel sound because h is silent.

Memory hook: Silent h invites an.

cards.term: Error: He is an university student.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is a university student.

Rule: University begins with consonant sound yu.

Memory hook: The sound is you, so use a.

cards.term: Error: He is an European scholar.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is a European scholar.

Rule: European begins with consonant sound yu.

Memory hook: European sounds like you-ropean.

cards.term: Error: He bought an one-rupee coin.
cards.definition:
Improved: He bought a one-rupee coin.

Rule: One begins with w sound.

Memory hook: One sounds like won, so use a.

cards.term: Error: She is a IAS officer.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is an IAS officer.

Rule: IAS begins with vowel sound eye.

Memory hook: Acronyms follow pronunciation.

cards.term: Error: He filed a FIR.
cards.definition:
Improved: He filed an FIR.

Rule: FIR begins with vowel sound ef.

Memory hook: Ef needs an.

cards.term: Error: He bought an useful tool.
cards.definition:
Improved: He bought a useful tool.

Rule: Useful begins with consonant sound yu.

Memory hook: Useful sounds like you-seful.

cards.term: Error: The honesty is the best policy.
cards.definition:
Improved: Honesty is the best policy.

Rule: Abstract nouns used generally take no article.

Memory hook: General values do not need the.

cards.term: Error: The gold is precious.
cards.definition:
Improved: Gold is precious.

Rule: Material nouns used generally take no article.

Memory hook: Gold in general stands alone.

cards.term: Error: The water is necessary for life.
cards.definition:
Improved: Water is necessary for life.

Rule: Uncountable nouns used generally take no article.

Memory hook: Water as a general idea needs no the.

cards.term: Error: I like the music.
cards.definition:
Improved: I like music.

Rule: Use no article when speaking generally about music.

Memory hook: Music in general needs no escort.

cards.term: Error: He plays guitar well.
cards.definition:
Improved: He plays the guitar well.

Rule: Use the before musical instruments after play.

Memory hook: Play the guitar, play cricket.

cards.term: Error: She plays the cricket every Sunday.
cards.definition:
Improved: She plays cricket every Sunday.

Rule: Games usually take no article.

Memory hook: Sports hate the.

cards.term: Error: He went to the school by bus.
cards.definition:
Improved: He went to school by bus.

Rule: Use no article when referring to the normal purpose of school.

Memory hook: Students go to school, visitors go to the school.

cards.term: Error: The teacher went to school to teach.
cards.definition:
Improved: The teacher went to school to teach.

Rule: No article is correct for institutional purpose.

Memory hook: Normal purpose removes the.

cards.term: Error: His father went to the school to meet the principal.
cards.definition:
Improved: His father went to the school to meet the principal.

Rule: Use the for a specific school building/visit.

Memory hook: A parent visits the school, a student goes to school.

cards.term: Error: He is in the hospital as a patient.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is in hospital as a patient.

Rule: In British/Indian usage, in hospital means as a patient.

Memory hook: Patient role often drops the.

cards.term: Error: I went to the hospital to meet him.
cards.definition:
Improved: I went to the hospital to meet him.

Rule: Use the when visiting a specific hospital.

Memory hook: Visitor points to the building.

cards.term: Error: He goes to bed at ten.
cards.definition:
Improved: He goes to bed at ten.

Rule: No article with go to bed as normal purpose.

Memory hook: Bed as sleep-purpose drops the.

cards.term: Error: He sat on bed near the window.
cards.definition:
Improved: He sat on the bed near the window.

Rule: Use the for a specific bed.

Memory hook: Specific object needs the.

cards.term: Error: The Delhi is the capital of India.
cards.definition:
Improved: Delhi is the capital of India.

Rule: City names usually take no article.

Memory hook: Cities stand like proper names.

cards.term: Error: The India is a large country.
cards.definition:
Improved: India is a large country.

Rule: Most country names take no article.

Memory hook: India needs no the.

cards.term: Error: Ganga is a holy river.
cards.definition:
Improved: The Ganga is a holy river.

Rule: Use the before river names.

Memory hook: Rivers usually flow with the.

cards.term: Error: Himalayas are snow-covered.
cards.definition:
Improved: The Himalayas are snow-covered.

Rule: Use the before mountain ranges.

Memory hook: Ranges take the, peaks usually do not.

cards.term: Error: The Mount Everest is the highest peak.
cards.definition:
Improved: Mount Everest is the highest peak.

Rule: Individual mountain peaks usually take no article.

Memory hook: Peak names stand alone.

cards.term: Error: Pacific Ocean is vast.
cards.definition:
Improved: The Pacific Ocean is vast.

Rule: Use the before oceans.

Memory hook: Oceans are too large to go article-less.

cards.term: Error: He reads Times of India daily.
cards.definition:
Improved: He reads The Times of India daily.

Rule: Many newspaper names take the.

Memory hook: Newspapers often arrive with the.

cards.term: Error: He is best player in the team.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is the best player in the team.

Rule: Use the with superlatives.

Memory hook: Best needs the crown.

cards.term: Error: This is same book.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is the same book.

Rule: Use the before same.

Memory hook: Same always wants the.

cards.term: Error: More you practise, better you become.
cards.definition:
Improved: The more you practise, the better you become.

Rule: Use the...the in parallel comparatives.

Memory hook: Two comparatives need two the's.

cards.term: Error: He is only son of his parents.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is the only son of his parents.

Rule: Use the before only when it makes the noun specific.

Memory hook: Only makes the noun unique.

cards.term: Error: He is a tallest boy in class.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is the tallest boy in class.

Rule: Use the with superlatives.

Memory hook: Tallest is a throne, not a random seat.

cards.term: Error: He is an unique person.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is a unique person.

Rule: Unique begins with consonant sound yu.

Memory hook: Unique sounds like you-neek.

cards.term: Error: This is a urgent matter.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is an urgent matter.

Rule: Urgent begins with vowel sound.

Memory hook: Urgent begins with uh, so use an.

cards.term: Error: He is senior than me.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is senior to me.

Rule: Senior takes to, not than.

Memory hook: Senior is not a normal comparative.

cards.term: Error: She is junior than her sister.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is junior to her sister.

Rule: Junior takes to.

Memory hook: Junior and senior travel with to.

cards.term: Error: This book is superior than that one.
cards.definition:
Improved: This book is superior to that one.

Rule: Superior takes to, not than.

Memory hook: Superior behaves like senior.

cards.term: Error: This cloth is inferior than that cloth.
cards.definition:
Improved: This cloth is inferior to that cloth.

Rule: Inferior takes to.

Memory hook: Inferior also joins the to-family.

cards.term: Error: He is married with a doctor.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is married to a doctor.

Rule: Married takes to.

Memory hook: Married to, not married with.

cards.term: Error: She is good in mathematics.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is good at mathematics.

Rule: Use good at for skills and subjects.

Memory hook: Skills sit at a point of ability.

cards.term: Error: He is weak at grammar.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is weak in grammar.

Rule: Use weak in for subjects or areas.

Memory hook: Weak in a subject.

cards.term: Error: He is suffering with fever.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is suffering from fever.

Rule: Suffer from disease.

Memory hook: Disease comes from, not with.

cards.term: Error: He died from cancer.
cards.definition:
Improved: He died of cancer.

Rule: Use die of diseases, die from external causes or effects.

Memory hook: Disease is usually die of.

cards.term: Error: He died of an accident.
cards.definition:
Improved: He died in an accident.

Rule: Use die in an accident.

Memory hook: Accidents are events you die in.

cards.term: Error: She is angry on me.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is angry with me.

Rule: Angry with a person.

Memory hook: Anger points with people.

cards.term: Error: He is angry with the delay.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is angry about the delay.

Rule: Angry about a thing or situation.

Memory hook: Use about for issues.

cards.term: Error: He is afraid from dogs.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is afraid of dogs.

Rule: Afraid takes of.

Memory hook: Fear belongs to of.

cards.term: Error: I am interested to learn English.
cards.definition:
Improved: I am interested in learning English.

Rule: Interested takes in plus gerund.

Memory hook: Interested in doing.

cards.term: Error: He insisted to go there.
cards.definition:
Improved: He insisted on going there.

Rule: Insist takes on plus gerund.

Memory hook: Insist stands on something.

cards.term: Error: She is fond to music.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is fond of music.

Rule: Fond takes of.

Memory hook: Fond of is fixed.

cards.term: Error: He is addicted with gaming.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is addicted to gaming.

Rule: Addicted takes to.

Memory hook: Addiction attaches to something.

cards.term: Error: This is different than mine.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is different from mine.

Rule: Different from is the standard exam form.

Memory hook: SSC usually prefers different from.

cards.term: Error: He is capable to solve it.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is capable of solving it.

Rule: Capable takes of plus gerund.

Memory hook: Capability belongs to of.

cards.term: Error: He is responsible of the mistake.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is responsible for the mistake.

Rule: Responsible for an action or mistake.

Memory hook: Blame and responsibility take for.

cards.term: Error: He is responsible for the manager.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is responsible to the manager.

Rule: Responsible to an authority, responsible for a task.

Memory hook: To authority, for duty.

cards.term: Error: She congratulated me for my success.
cards.definition:
Improved: She congratulated me on my success.

Rule: Congratulate on success.

Memory hook: Congratulations sit on the occasion.

cards.term: Error: He blamed me of the loss.
cards.definition:
Improved: He blamed me for the loss.

Rule: Blame someone for something.

Memory hook: Blame needs for.

cards.term: Error: He accused me for theft.
cards.definition:
Improved: He accused me of theft.

Rule: Accuse someone of an offence.

Memory hook: Accusation uses of.

cards.term: Error: She prevented me to enter.
cards.definition:
Improved: She prevented me from entering.

Rule: Prevent takes from plus gerund.

Memory hook: Prevent blocks from doing.

cards.term: Error: He refrained to speak.
cards.definition:
Improved: He refrained from speaking.

Rule: Refrain takes from plus gerund.

Memory hook: Refrain means hold back from.

cards.term: Error: You must comply to the rules.
cards.definition:
Improved: You must comply with the rules.

Rule: Comply takes with.

Memory hook: Rules are complied with.

cards.term: Error: He objected against the proposal.
cards.definition:
Improved: He objected to the proposal.

Rule: Object takes to.

Memory hook: Object to, not against.

cards.term: Error: Refer this dictionary.
cards.definition:
Improved: Refer to this dictionary.

Rule: Refer takes to when meaning consult.

Memory hook: Refer to a source.

cards.term: Error: He resembles to his father.
cards.definition:
Improved: He resembles his father.

Rule: Resemble takes no preposition.

Memory hook: Resemble is directly transitive.

cards.term: Error: Discuss about the matter.
cards.definition:
Improved: Discuss the matter.

Rule: Discuss takes a direct object, no about.

Memory hook: Discuss already includes about.

cards.term: Error: He entered into the room.
cards.definition:
Improved: He entered the room.

Rule: Enter takes direct object for places.

Memory hook: Enter already means go into.

cards.term: Error: They reached to the station.
cards.definition:
Improved: They reached the station.

Rule: Reach takes direct object, no to.

Memory hook: Reach is direct.

cards.term: Error: She requested for help.
cards.definition:
Improved: She requested help.

Rule: Request as a verb takes direct object.

Memory hook: Request does not need for before object.

cards.term: Error: He approached to the officer.
cards.definition:
Improved: He approached the officer.

Rule: Approach takes direct object.

Memory hook: Approach means go to, so no extra to.

cards.term: Error: He ordered for tea.
cards.definition:
Improved: He ordered tea.

Rule: Order takes direct object when asking for food/item.

Memory hook: Do not overfeed order with for.

cards.term: Error: He lacks of confidence.
cards.definition:
Improved: He lacks confidence.

Rule: Lack as verb takes direct object.

Memory hook: Lack needs no of.

cards.term: Error: He is lacking in confidence.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is lacking in confidence.

Rule: Lacking in is correct as adjective-like use.

Memory hook: Lack confidence, but lacking in confidence.

cards.term: Error: She is looking forward for meeting you.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is looking forward to meeting you.

Rule: Look forward to takes gerund.

Memory hook: The to is a preposition.

cards.term: Error: He is familiar to this topic.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is familiar with this topic.

Rule: Familiar with a subject.

Memory hook: You are familiar with, not familiar to.

cards.term: Error: This topic is familiar with me.
cards.definition:
Improved: This topic is familiar to me.

Rule: A thing is familiar to a person.

Memory hook: Person familiar with thing, thing familiar to person.

cards.term: Error: He is more taller than his brother.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is taller than his brother.

Rule: Do not use more with an -er comparative.

Memory hook: One comparative is enough.

cards.term: Error: She is more wiser than before.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is wiser than before.

Rule: Avoid double comparative.

Memory hook: More wiser is like wearing two helmets.

cards.term: Error: This is the most easiest question.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is the easiest question.

Rule: Avoid double superlative.

Memory hook: Most easiest is over-decoration.

cards.term: Error: He is the most cleverest boy.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is the cleverest boy.

Rule: Do not combine most with -est.

Memory hook: Superlative needs one crown.

cards.term: Error: She is senior than me.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is senior to me.

Rule: Senior takes to, not than.

Memory hook: Senior is comparative in meaning but not structure.

cards.term: Error: He is junior than I.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is junior to me.

Rule: Junior takes to.

Memory hook: Junior belongs to the to-family.

cards.term: Error: This book is preferable than that one.
cards.definition:
Improved: This book is preferable to that one.

Rule: Preferable takes to.

Memory hook: Preferable behaves like superior.

cards.term: Error: I prefer tea than coffee.
cards.definition:
Improved: I prefer tea to coffee.

Rule: Prefer takes to, not than.

Memory hook: Prefer A to B.

cards.term: Error: He is as tall than his brother.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is as tall as his brother.

Rule: Use as...as for equality.

Memory hook: As needs its twin.

cards.term: Error: She is not so tall as her sister.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is not so tall as her sister.

Rule: Not so...as is correct in negative comparison.

Memory hook: Negative equality often uses so...as.

cards.term: Error: She is not as tall than her sister.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is not as tall as her sister.

Rule: Use as...as, not as...than.

Memory hook: Do not mix comparison families.

cards.term: Error: He is taller from his friend.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is taller than his friend.

Rule: Comparative adjectives take than.

Memory hook: Taller needs than.

cards.term: Error: This is better than any book.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is better than any other book.

Rule: When comparing one item with its own group, use any other.

Memory hook: The item cannot be compared with itself.

cards.term: Error: Mumbai is larger than any city in Maharashtra.
cards.definition:
Improved: Mumbai is larger than any other city in Maharashtra.

Rule: Use any other when the city is part of the same state.

Memory hook: Do not make Mumbai compete with itself.

cards.term: Error: He is the best of the two brothers.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is the better of the two brothers.

Rule: Use comparative for two, superlative for more than two.

Memory hook: Two people need better, not best.

cards.term: Error: Of the three options, this is better.
cards.definition:
Improved: Of the three options, this is the best.

Rule: Use superlative among three or more.

Memory hook: Three options need the crown form.

cards.term: Error: This is one of the best book.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is one of the best books.

Rule: One of the is followed by plural noun.

Memory hook: One of many best books.

cards.term: Error: She is one of the most intelligent girl.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is one of the most intelligent girls.

Rule: One of the takes plural noun.

Memory hook: One among many girls.

cards.term: Error: The higher you climb, colder it gets.
cards.definition:
Improved: The higher you climb, the colder it gets.

Rule: Use the...the in proportional comparison.

Memory hook: Two linked changes need two the's.

cards.term: Error: More he earns, more he spends.
cards.definition:
Improved: The more he earns, the more he spends.

Rule: Use the...the structure.

Memory hook: Income and spending rise together with the...the.

cards.term: Error: He is stronger than brave.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is more strong than brave.

Rule: When comparing two qualities in the same person, use more + adjective than + adjective.

Memory hook: Same person, two qualities, use more...than.

cards.term: Error: She is wiser than intelligent.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is more wise than intelligent.

Rule: For two qualities in one person, use more...than.

Memory hook: Compare qualities, not people.

cards.term: Error: This is less better than that.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is worse than that.

Rule: Less better is incorrect and awkward.

Memory hook: Better has an opposite, use worse.

cards.term: Error: He is comparatively better.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is better.

Rule: Comparatively already implies comparison and is often redundant with better in correction questions.

Memory hook: Better already compares.

cards.term: Error: This is relatively more easier.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is relatively easier.

Rule: Avoid double comparative with more easier.

Memory hook: Easier already has comparison built in.

cards.term: Error: He is as good if not better than his brother.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is as good as, if not better than, his brother.

Rule: Use complete comparison structure with as good as.

Memory hook: The first comparison needs its second as.

cards.term: Error: He is no less intelligent than you.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is no less intelligent than you.

Rule: This is correct and means equally intelligent or not inferior.

Memory hook: No less than can be a valid emphatic comparison.

cards.term: Error: She is no better than a thief.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is no better than a thief.

Rule: This is correct idiom meaning equally bad.

Memory hook: No better than is an idiomatic judgment.

cards.term: Error: He is elder than me.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is older than I am / He is older than me.

Rule: Older is generally used with than, elder is used before family nouns.

Memory hook: Elder brother, but older than me.

cards.term: Error: My elder brother is older than me.
cards.definition:
Improved: My elder brother is older than me.

Rule: Elder before brother is correct, older for comparison is correct.

Memory hook: Elder labels family rank, older compares age.

cards.term: Error: Between you and I, this plan is risky.
cards.definition:
Improved: Between you and me, this plan is risky.

Rule: After prepositions, use object case me.

Memory hook: Between always takes object case.

cards.term: Error: He is taller than me.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is taller than I am.

Rule: Formal comparison uses subject case when verb is implied.

Memory hook: Than I am is formal and precise.

cards.term: Error: Everyone should do their duty.
cards.definition:
Improved: Everyone should do his or her duty.

Rule: Traditional exam grammar treats everyone as singular.

Memory hook: Modern usage accepts their, but SSC-style grammar may expect singular agreement.

cards.term: Error: Each student must bring their admit card.
cards.definition:
Improved: Each student must bring his or her admit card.

Rule: Each is singular in traditional grammar.

Memory hook: Each is one student at a time.

cards.term: Error: Neither of the boys did their homework.
cards.definition:
Improved: Neither of the boys did his homework.

Rule: Neither is singular in traditional exam grammar.

Memory hook: Neither points to not one.

cards.term: Error: The team won their match.
cards.definition:
Improved: The team won its match.

Rule: A collective noun as one unit takes singular pronoun.

Memory hook: One team, one its.

cards.term: Error: The committee submitted their report.
cards.definition:
Improved: The committee submitted its report.

Rule: Committee as one body takes its.

Memory hook: If it acts as one body, use its.

cards.term: Error: Me and my friend went there.
cards.definition:
Improved: My friend and I went there.

Rule: Use subject pronoun I and put yourself last.

Memory hook: Polite grammar sends I to the end.

cards.term: Error: Him and I are brothers.
cards.definition:
Improved: He and I are brothers.

Rule: Use subject pronouns before the verb.

Memory hook: Subjects need he, not him.

cards.term: Error: She is more intelligent than him.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is more intelligent than he is.

Rule: Formal comparison uses subject case with implied verb.

Memory hook: Than he is avoids ambiguity.

cards.term: Error: This is between he and I.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is between him and me.

Rule: Between is a preposition and takes object case.

Memory hook: Between him and me is the exam-safe phrase.

cards.term: Error: The teacher praised Riya and I.
cards.definition:
Improved: The teacher praised Riya and me.

Rule: Object of praised should be me.

Memory hook: Remove Riya and check: praised me.

cards.term: Error: They invited my brother and I.
cards.definition:
Improved: They invited my brother and me.

Rule: Object position needs me.

Memory hook: Test it alone: invited me.

cards.term: Error: Let you and I solve it.
cards.definition:
Improved: Let you and me solve it.

Rule: After let, the object pronoun is needed.

Memory hook: Let me, not let I.

cards.term: Error: This is him who helped me.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is he who helped me.

Rule: After be, formal grammar often uses subject complement he.

Memory hook: Formal identity after is takes he.

cards.term: Error: It was me who called you.
cards.definition:
Improved: It was I who called you.

Rule: Formal grammar uses subject form after it was.

Memory hook: SSC may prefer it was I.

cards.term: Error: He himself did the work.
cards.definition:
Improved: He himself did the work.

Rule: This is correct for emphasis.

Memory hook: Himself adds emphasis, not error.

cards.term: Error: He did the work hisself.
cards.definition:
Improved: He did the work himself.

Rule: Correct reflexive form is himself.

Memory hook: Hisself is non-standard.

cards.term: Error: She blamed her for the mistake.
cards.definition:
Improved: She blamed herself for the mistake.

Rule: Use reflexive pronoun when subject and object are same person.

Memory hook: If she blamed she, use herself.

cards.term: Error: I enjoyed at the party.
cards.definition:
Improved: I enjoyed myself at the party.

Rule: Enjoy needs an object when used this way.

Memory hook: Enjoy yourself, not simply enjoy at.

cards.term: Error: They availed the opportunity.
cards.definition:
Improved: They availed themselves of the opportunity.

Rule: Avail oneself of is the formal phrase.

Memory hook: Avail needs oneself in this structure.

cards.term: Error: He absented from class.
cards.definition:
Improved: He absented himself from class.

Rule: Absent as a verb often takes reflexive object.

Memory hook: He absented himself.

cards.term: Error: You should pride of your work.
cards.definition:
Improved: You should pride yourself on your work.

Rule: Use pride oneself on.

Memory hook: Pride yourself on, not pride of.

cards.term: Error: The dog wagged it's tail.
cards.definition:
Improved: The dog wagged its tail.

Rule: Its is possessive, it's means it is.

Memory hook: A tail belongs to its, not it is.

cards.term: Error: Whom do you think will win?
cards.definition:
Improved: Who do you think will win?

Rule: Who is subject of will win.

Memory hook: Ask: who will win.

cards.term: Error: Who did you meet yesterday?
cards.definition:
Improved: Whom did you meet yesterday?

Rule: Formal grammar uses whom as object.

Memory hook: Meet takes an object.

cards.term: Error: Whose is this book?
cards.definition:
Improved: Whose book is this?

Rule: Use whose before the noun in this structure.

Memory hook: Whose book sounds natural and correct.

cards.term: Error: One should respect his parents.
cards.definition:
Improved: One should respect one's parents.

Rule: Pronoun should agree with one in formal grammar.

Memory hook: One pairs with one's.

cards.term: Error: Somebody left their bag here.
cards.definition:
Improved: Somebody left his or her bag here.

Rule: Traditional grammar treats somebody as singular.

Memory hook: Somebody is one unknown person.

cards.term: Error: The two sisters love one another.
cards.definition:
Improved: The two sisters love each other.

Rule: Each other is preferred for two, one another for more than two.

Memory hook: Two people exchange each other.

cards.term: Error: Return back the book tomorrow.
cards.definition:
Improved: Return the book tomorrow.

Rule: Return already means give back.

Memory hook: Back is packed inside return.

cards.term: Error: Repeat it again.
cards.definition:
Improved: Repeat it.

Rule: Repeat already means say or do again.

Memory hook: Again repeats repeat.

cards.term: Error: Revert back to me soon.
cards.definition:
Improved: Revert to me soon.

Rule: Revert already means return/respond in common office usage.

Memory hook: Back is redundant after revert.

cards.term: Error: Discuss about the issue.
cards.definition:
Improved: Discuss the issue.

Rule: Discuss already means talk about.

Memory hook: About is extra luggage.

cards.term: Error: Enter into the room quietly.
cards.definition:
Improved: Enter the room quietly.

Rule: Enter already means go into.

Memory hook: Into is hidden inside enter.

cards.term: Error: He ordered for a coffee.
cards.definition:
Improved: He ordered a coffee.

Rule: Order takes direct object.

Memory hook: Food orders do not need for.

cards.term: Error: She requested for a leave.
cards.definition:
Improved: She requested leave.

Rule: Request as a verb takes direct object.

Memory hook: Request does not need for before the object.

cards.term: Error: The reason is because he was late.
cards.definition:
Improved: The reason is that he was late.

Rule: Use reason is that, not reason is because.

Memory hook: Reason and because duplicate cause logic.

cards.term: Error: The reason why is because he forgot.
cards.definition:
Improved: The reason is that he forgot.

Rule: Avoid reason why plus because redundancy.

Memory hook: Do not stack three cause markers.

cards.term: Error: He returned back again.
cards.definition:
Improved: He returned.

Rule: Back and again are redundant with returned.

Memory hook: This sentence is a redundancy festival.

cards.term: Error: I saw it with my own eyes.
cards.definition:
Improved: I saw it.

Rule: With my own eyes is often redundant unless used for emphasis.

Memory hook: Seeing normally uses eyes, not elbows.

cards.term: Error: He is a very unique person.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is a unique person.

Rule: Unique means one of a kind, so very is usually unnecessary.

Memory hook: Unique does not need a volume button.

cards.term: Error: The two twins look alike.
cards.definition:
Improved: The twins look alike.

Rule: Twins already means two.

Memory hook: Two twins technically means four people.

cards.term: Error: The final conclusion is clear.
cards.definition:
Improved: The conclusion is clear.

Rule: Conclusion already means final result.

Memory hook: Final is built into conclusion.

cards.term: Error: He gave a free gift.
cards.definition:
Improved: He gave a gift.

Rule: A gift is normally free.

Memory hook: Paid gift is a shopkeeper's magic trick.

cards.term: Error: The meeting was postponed to a later date.
cards.definition:
Improved: The meeting was postponed.

Rule: Postponed already means moved to a later time.

Memory hook: Later date is inside postponed.

cards.term: Error: He is my cousin brother.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is my cousin.

Rule: Cousin already indicates relation, do not add brother/sister in formal English.

Memory hook: Cousin brother is Indian English, not exam-safe standard English.

cards.term: Error: She is my cousin sister.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is my cousin.

Rule: Use cousin for both male and female cousins.

Memory hook: Cousin does the job alone.

cards.term: Error: The actual fact is different.
cards.definition:
Improved: The fact is different.

Rule: Fact already implies actuality.

Memory hook: Actual fact is overfed.

cards.term: Error: He added an additional point.
cards.definition:
Improved: He added a point.

Rule: Added and additional repeat the same idea.

Memory hook: Additional has already joined add.

cards.term: Error: They planned in advance.
cards.definition:
Improved: They planned.

Rule: Planning is normally done in advance.

Memory hook: Planning after the event is an excuse.

cards.term: Error: He shouted loudly.
cards.definition:
Improved: He shouted.

Rule: Shout already means speak loudly.

Memory hook: A whisper can be soft, a shout cannot.

cards.term: Error: She whispered softly.
cards.definition:
Improved: She whispered.

Rule: Whisper already means speak softly.

Memory hook: Softly hides inside whisper.

cards.term: Error: The small tiny insect flew away.
cards.definition:
Improved: The tiny insect flew away.

Rule: Small and tiny repeat the same meaning.

Memory hook: Use one size adjective.

cards.term: Error: He is completely full.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is full.

Rule: Full already means completely filled.

Memory hook: A full glass cannot be more full in ordinary use.

cards.term: Error: They surrounded him on all sides.
cards.definition:
Improved: They surrounded him.

Rule: Surround means enclose on all sides.

Memory hook: All sides is built into surround.

cards.term: Error: He is an old veteran.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is a veteran.

Rule: Veteran already suggests long experience.

Memory hook: Veteran has age of experience inside it.

cards.term: Error: The past history of India is rich.
cards.definition:
Improved: The history of India is rich.

Rule: History already concerns the past.

Memory hook: Past history is usually redundant.

cards.term: Error: He made a new innovation.
cards.definition:
Improved: He made an innovation.

Rule: Innovation already means something new.

Memory hook: New innovation is like wet water.

cards.term: Error: Please prepay in advance.
cards.definition:
Improved: Please prepay.

Rule: Prepay means pay in advance.

Memory hook: Advance is already in prepay.

cards.term: Error: They cooperated together.
cards.definition:
Improved: They cooperated.

Rule: Cooperate means work together.

Memory hook: Together is inside cooperate.

cards.term: Error: The end result was surprising.
cards.definition:
Improved: The result was surprising.

Rule: Result already means outcome/end.

Memory hook: End result is usually redundant.

cards.term: Error: He followed after me.
cards.definition:
Improved: He followed me.

Rule: Follow already means come after.

Memory hook: After is hiding inside follow.

cards.term: Error: The basic fundamentals are clear.
cards.definition:
Improved: The fundamentals are clear.

Rule: Fundamentals are basic principles.

Memory hook: Basic fundamentals repeats itself.

cards.term: Error: Although he was tired, but he continued.
cards.definition:
Improved: Although he was tired, he continued.

Rule: Do not use although and but together.

Memory hook: Although already does the contrast work.

cards.term: Error: Though it was raining, but we went out.
cards.definition:
Improved: Though it was raining, we went out.

Rule: Though and but should not be paired in the same clause.

Memory hook: One contrast marker is enough.

cards.term: Error: Because he was ill, so he stayed home.
cards.definition:
Improved: Because he was ill, he stayed home.

Rule: Do not use because and so together.

Memory hook: Because gives the cause, so is not needed.

cards.term: Error: As he was late, so he missed the bus.
cards.definition:
Improved: As he was late, he missed the bus.

Rule: As meaning because does not need so.

Memory hook: Cause is already marked by as.

cards.term: Error: No sooner he reached than it rained.
cards.definition:
Improved: No sooner did he reach than it rained.

Rule: No sooner at the start takes inversion with did.

Memory hook: No sooner demands question-like word order.

cards.term: Error: No sooner had he reached when it rained.
cards.definition:
Improved: No sooner had he reached than it rained.

Rule: No sooner pairs with than.

Memory hook: No sooner than, hardly when.

cards.term: Error: Hardly he had reached when the bell rang.
cards.definition:
Improved: Hardly had he reached when the bell rang.

Rule: Hardly at the beginning takes inversion.

Memory hook: Hardly pulls the helping verb forward.

cards.term: Error: Hardly had he reached than the bell rang.
cards.definition:
Improved: Hardly had he reached when the bell rang.

Rule: Hardly pairs with when.

Memory hook: Hardly when, no sooner than.

cards.term: Error: Scarcely had he entered than everyone stood up.
cards.definition:
Improved: Scarcely had he entered when everyone stood up.

Rule: Scarcely pairs with when.

Memory hook: Scarcely behaves like hardly.

cards.term: Error: Not only he sings but also dances.
cards.definition:
Improved: Not only does he sing, but he also dances.

Rule: Not only at the beginning takes inversion.

Memory hook: Not only makes the sentence flip.

cards.term: Error: He is both intelligent as well as hardworking.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is both intelligent and hardworking.

Rule: Both pairs with and.

Memory hook: Both and is the correct pair.

cards.term: Error: She is either intelligent nor hardworking.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is either intelligent or hardworking.

Rule: Either pairs with or.

Memory hook: Either-or is one family.

cards.term: Error: Neither he nor his friends was present.
cards.definition:
Improved: Neither he nor his friends were present.

Rule: With neither...nor, verb agrees with the nearer subject friends.

Memory hook: Nearest subject wins.

cards.term: Error: Neither his friends nor he were present.
cards.definition:
Improved: Neither his friends nor he was present.

Rule: Verb agrees with nearer subject he.

Memory hook: Nor passes the verb to the neighbour.

cards.term: Error: He is not only wise but also honest.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is not only wise but also honest.

Rule: This is correct parallel structure.

Memory hook: Not only...but also is balanced here.

cards.term: Error: He not only lost his bag but also his ticket.
cards.definition:
Improved: He lost not only his bag but also his ticket.

Rule: Place not only before the first parallel item.

Memory hook: Keep the two compared items parallel.

cards.term: Error: She is neither rich or famous.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is neither rich nor famous.

Rule: Neither pairs with nor.

Memory hook: Neither-nor, not neither-or.

cards.term: Error: He is so weak that he cannot walk.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is so weak that he cannot walk.

Rule: This is correct so...that structure.

Memory hook: So shows degree, that shows result.

cards.term: Error: He is too weak that he cannot walk.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is too weak to walk.

Rule: Too takes to-infinitive, not that-clause.

Memory hook: Too means excess, then to follows.

cards.term: Error: He is enough strong to lift it.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is strong enough to lift it.

Rule: Enough comes after adjective.

Memory hook: Adjective first, enough second.

cards.term: Error: He is too much tired to work.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is too tired to work.

Rule: Use too before adjectives, not too much.

Memory hook: Too much is for nouns or verbs, too is for adjectives.

cards.term: Error: He worked hard so that he may pass.
cards.definition:
Improved: He worked hard so that he might pass.

Rule: With past main verb, may usually changes to might.

Memory hook: Past work pulls may to might.

cards.term: Error: Work hard lest you should fail.
cards.definition:
Improved: Work hard lest you fail / Work hard lest you should fail.

Rule: Lest may be followed by should or bare subjunctive.

Memory hook: Do not use not after lest.

cards.term: Error: Work hard lest you should not fail.
cards.definition:
Improved: Work hard lest you should fail.

Rule: Lest already means for fear that not.

Memory hook: Lest already contains the negative idea.

cards.term: Error: Unless you do not study, you will fail.
cards.definition:
Improved: Unless you study, you will fail.

Rule: Unless already means if not, so do not is redundant.

Memory hook: Unless carries the not inside it.

cards.term: Error: Until you do not finish, you cannot leave.
cards.definition:
Improved: Until you finish, you cannot leave.

Rule: Until should not be followed by not in this structure.

Memory hook: Until waits for the positive event.

cards.term: Error: He is such weak that he cannot walk.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is so weak that he cannot walk.

Rule: Use so with adjective, such with noun phrase.

Memory hook: So weak, such a weak man.

cards.term: Error: He is so a good man that everyone likes him.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is such a good man that everyone likes him.

Rule: Use such before adjective + noun.

Memory hook: Such carries the noun phrase.

cards.term: Error: He is as clever if not cleverer than his brother.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is as clever as, if not cleverer than, his brother.

Rule: Complete the as...as structure.

Memory hook: The first comparison needs its missing as.

cards.term: Error: He is rather intelligent than hardworking.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is more intelligent than hardworking.

Rule: Use more...than when comparing qualities.

Memory hook: Rather is not the comparison engine here.

cards.term: Error: She only gave me five rupees.
cards.definition:
Improved: She gave me only five rupees.

Rule: Place only near the word it modifies.

Memory hook: Only is a spotlight, put it on the right word.

cards.term: Error: Only he lent me his book.
cards.definition:
Improved: Only he lent me his book.

Rule: This is correct if the meaning is nobody else lent it.

Memory hook: Only changes meaning by position.

cards.term: Error: He nearly drove the car for six hours.
cards.definition:
Improved: He drove the car for nearly six hours.

Rule: Nearly should modify six hours, not drove.

Memory hook: Nearly six hours means almost six hours.

cards.term: Error: I almost have finished the work.
cards.definition:
Improved: I have almost finished the work.

Rule: Almost usually goes before the main verb or adjective it modifies.

Memory hook: Almost should sit near finished.

cards.term: Error: He even did not apologise.
cards.definition:
Improved: He did not even apologise.

Rule: Even should be placed near the emphasized action.

Memory hook: Not even is a strong pair.

cards.term: Error: She hardly works hard.
cards.definition:
Improved: She hardly works.

Rule: Hardly means almost not, do not combine awkwardly with hard unless intended.

Memory hook: Hardly hard creates comic confusion.

cards.term: Error: The teacher explained the rule clearly.
cards.definition:
Improved: The teacher explained the rule clearly.

Rule: This is correct adverb placement.

Memory hook: Clearly explains the manner of explaining.

cards.term: Error: He speaks English fluent.
cards.definition:
Improved: He speaks English fluently.

Rule: Use adverb fluently to modify speaks.

Memory hook: Verbs need adverbs, not adjectives.

cards.term: Error: She sings sweet.
cards.definition:
Improved: She sings sweetly.

Rule: Use adverb sweetly to modify sings.

Memory hook: Singing needs sweetly.

cards.term: Error: He runs quick.
cards.definition:
Improved: He runs quickly.

Rule: Use adverb quickly to modify runs.

Memory hook: Running is an action, so use an adverb.

cards.term: Error: This is a beautifully flower.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is a beautiful flower.

Rule: Use adjective beautiful before noun flower.

Memory hook: Nouns need adjectives.

cards.term: Error: She is a well girl.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is a healthy girl.

Rule: Well usually means in good health after be, but healthy is clearer before noun.

Memory hook: A well girl sounds awkward in standard usage.

cards.term: Error: He performed good.
cards.definition:
Improved: He performed well.

Rule: Use well as adverb for performance.

Memory hook: Good describes nouns, well describes actions.

cards.term: Error: She looks beautifully.
cards.definition:
Improved: She looks beautiful.

Rule: Linking verbs take adjectives, not adverbs.

Memory hook: Looks connects to a state, not an action.

cards.term: Error: The soup tastes deliciously.
cards.definition:
Improved: The soup tastes delicious.

Rule: Taste as linking verb takes adjective.

Memory hook: Soup is delicious, it does not taste deliciously.

cards.term: Error: The flower smells sweetly.
cards.definition:
Improved: The flower smells sweet.

Rule: Smell as linking verb takes adjective.

Memory hook: Flowers smell sweet, not sweetly.

cards.term: Error: He feels badly about it.
cards.definition:
Improved: He feels bad about it.

Rule: Feel as emotional state takes adjective bad.

Memory hook: Feeling bad is emotion, feeling badly is poor touch-sense.

cards.term: Error: The child slept sound.
cards.definition:
Improved: The child slept soundly.

Rule: Sleep is an action verb here, so use adverb soundly.

Memory hook: Sleep needs an adverb when describing manner.

cards.term: Error: He returned back quickly.
cards.definition:
Improved: He returned quickly.

Rule: Back is redundant after returned.

Memory hook: Quickly can stay, back must leave.

cards.term: Error: I saw a man walking on the road with a telescope.
cards.definition:
Improved: With a telescope, I saw a man walking on the road.

Rule: Place modifier clearly to avoid ambiguity.

Memory hook: Otherwise the man may look like he owns the telescope.

cards.term: Error: Running down the street, the bag fell from him.
cards.definition:
Improved: Running down the street, he dropped the bag.

Rule: Avoid dangling modifier. The person, not the bag, was running.

Memory hook: Bags do not usually sprint by themselves.

cards.term: Error: Being rainy, we cancelled the match.
cards.definition:
Improved: As it was rainy, we cancelled the match.

Rule: Avoid dangling participle. It, not we, was rainy.

Memory hook: People are not rainy, weather is.

cards.term: Error: Walking to school, a dog chased him.
cards.definition:
Improved: While he was walking to school, a dog chased him.

Rule: Make the doer of the opening phrase clear.

Memory hook: A dog did not walk him to school.

cards.term: Error: Having finished the work, the TV was switched on.
cards.definition:
Improved: Having finished the work, he switched on the TV.

Rule: The doer of having finished must be the subject.

Memory hook: TVs rarely finish homework.

cards.term: Error: To improve marks, grammar must be practised.
cards.definition:
Improved: To improve marks, students must practise grammar.

Rule: The subject should logically perform the action.

Memory hook: Grammar does not improve marks by itself.

cards.term: Error: The man was wearing a black leather old jacket.
cards.definition:
Improved: The man was wearing an old black leather jacket.

Rule: Adjective order usually follows opinion/age/colour/material/noun.

Memory hook: Age comes before colour and material.

cards.term: Error: She bought a red beautiful dress.
cards.definition:
Improved: She bought a beautiful red dress.

Rule: Opinion adjective usually comes before colour.

Memory hook: Beautiful comes before red.

cards.term: Error: He gave me a wooden small box.
cards.definition:
Improved: He gave me a small wooden box.

Rule: Size usually comes before material.

Memory hook: Small before wooden sounds natural.

cards.term: Error: I have never seen such a beautiful scenery.
cards.definition:
Improved: I have never seen such beautiful scenery.

Rule: Scenery is uncountable, so do not use a.

Memory hook: Scenery is a mass noun.

cards.term: Error: He gave me many advice.
cards.definition:
Improved: He gave me much advice / He gave me many pieces of advice.

Rule: Advice is uncountable.

Memory hook: Advice needs much or pieces.

cards.term: Error: She likes singing, dancing and to paint.
cards.definition:
Improved: She likes singing, dancing and painting.

Rule: Keep items in a list grammatically parallel.

Memory hook: A list should march in the same uniform.

cards.term: Error: He is honest, hardworking and a man of courage.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is honest, hardworking and courageous.

Rule: Keep adjective list parallel.

Memory hook: Do not mix adjectives with a noun phrase awkwardly.

cards.term: Error: She wants to study, to work and travelling.
cards.definition:
Improved: She wants to study, to work and to travel.

Rule: Keep infinitives parallel.

Memory hook: Parallel structure is grammar symmetry.

cards.term: Error: He came, saw and was conquering.
cards.definition:
Improved: He came, saw and conquered.

Rule: Keep verb forms parallel.

Memory hook: Caesar did not say came, saw, was conquering.

cards.term: Error: The job needs patience, skill and to work hard.
cards.definition:
Improved: The job needs patience, skill and hard work.

Rule: Keep nouns parallel.

Memory hook: Patience, skill and hard work belong to one noun family.

cards.term: Error: She is not only intelligent but also has courage.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is not only intelligent but also courageous.

Rule: Keep both sides of not only...but also parallel.

Memory hook: Both sides should wear the same grammar clothes.

cards.term: Error: He not only helped me but also my brother.
cards.definition:
Improved: He helped not only me but also my brother.

Rule: Place not only before the first parallel item.

Memory hook: The pair should compare me and my brother.

cards.term: Error: I would rather walk than running.
cards.definition:
Improved: I would rather walk than run.

Rule: Would rather takes base verb on both sides.

Memory hook: Walk and run must match.

cards.term: Error: He prefers reading than to write.
cards.definition:
Improved: He prefers reading to writing.

Rule: Prefer takes to and parallel gerunds.

Memory hook: Reading pairs with writing.

cards.term: Error: She is interested in singing and to dance.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is interested in singing and dancing.

Rule: Preposition in takes gerund after it.

Memory hook: In singing and dancing keeps it parallel.

cards.term: Error: He is capable of solving and to explain it.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is capable of solving and explaining it.

Rule: Of takes gerund, so both verbs should be gerunds.

Memory hook: After of, keep -ing.

cards.term: Error: They discussed the plan, the budget and how to execute it.
cards.definition:
Improved: They discussed the plan, the budget and the execution strategy.

Rule: Keep list items parallel.

Memory hook: Noun, noun, noun is cleaner.

cards.term: Error: The aim is to educate, to empower and creating awareness.
cards.definition:
Improved: The aim is to educate, to empower and to create awareness.

Rule: Keep infinitive structure parallel.

Memory hook: To educate, to empower, to create.

cards.term: Error: She is known for her honesty, discipline and being punctual.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is known for her honesty, discipline and punctuality.

Rule: Use noun forms in a list.

Memory hook: Honesty, discipline, punctuality sound balanced.

cards.term: Error: He is both a good teacher and teaches well.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is both a good teacher and a good speaker.

Rule: Both...and should connect matching structures.

Memory hook: Both sides need the same grammatical weight.

cards.term: Error: Either work hard or you should leave.
cards.definition:
Improved: Either work hard or leave.

Rule: Keep alternatives parallel after either...or.

Memory hook: Either do this or do that.

cards.term: Error: Neither the plan was useful nor practical.
cards.definition:
Improved: The plan was neither useful nor practical.

Rule: Place neither before the first parallel adjective.

Memory hook: Neither useful nor practical is balanced.

cards.term: Error: He is too tired and cannot work.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is too tired to work.

Rule: Too...to is the correct structure.

Memory hook: Too tired naturally asks for to work.

cards.term: Error: He is so tired to work.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is so tired that he cannot work.

Rule: So...that expresses result.

Memory hook: So tired needs that, too tired needs to.

cards.term: Error: She is enough wise to decide.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is wise enough to decide.

Rule: Enough follows adjective.

Memory hook: Wise enough, not enough wise.

cards.term: Error: The problem is easy to solve it.
cards.definition:
Improved: The problem is easy to solve.

Rule: Do not repeat the object after an infinitive adjective structure.

Memory hook: Problem is already the object of solve.

cards.term: Error: This book is worth to read.
cards.definition:
Improved: This book is worth reading.

Rule: Worth takes gerund.

Memory hook: Worth reading is the fixed form.

cards.term: Error: It is no use to argue.
cards.definition:
Improved: It is no use arguing.

Rule: No use takes gerund.

Memory hook: No use arguing, not no use to argue.

cards.term: Error: There is no point to wait.
cards.definition:
Improved: There is no point in waiting.

Rule: No point takes in plus gerund.

Memory hook: Point in waiting is fixed.

cards.term: Error: He had difficulty to find the address.
cards.definition:
Improved: He had difficulty in finding the address.

Rule: Difficulty is followed by in plus gerund.

Memory hook: Difficulty in doing.

cards.term: Error: She has no objection to work late.
cards.definition:
Improved: She has no objection to working late.

Rule: To is a preposition after objection.

Memory hook: Objection to doing.

cards.term: Error: He devoted his life to serve the poor.
cards.definition:
Improved: He devoted his life to serving the poor.

Rule: Devote to takes gerund.

Memory hook: Devoted to doing.

cards.term: Error: She confessed to steal the money.
cards.definition:
Improved: She confessed to stealing the money.

Rule: Confess to takes gerund.

Memory hook: Confess to doing.

cards.term: Error: He is addicted to play games.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is addicted to playing games.

Rule: Addicted to takes gerund.

Memory hook: Addicted to doing.

cards.term: Error: I am looking forward to see you.
cards.definition:
Improved: I am looking forward to seeing you.

Rule: Look forward to takes gerund.

Memory hook: This to is not infinitive.

cards.term: Error: He made a blunder mistake.
cards.definition:
Improved: He made a blunder.

Rule: Blunder already means a serious mistake.

Memory hook: Blunder contains mistake inside it.

cards.term: Error: He gave me a good advice.
cards.definition:
Improved: He gave me good advice.

Rule: Advice is uncountable, so do not use a.

Memory hook: Advice refuses a.

cards.term: Error: He gave me an advice.
cards.definition:
Improved: He gave me a piece of advice.

Rule: Use a piece of advice for one item of advice.

Memory hook: Advice needs a piece if you count it.

cards.term: Error: He has many furnitures.
cards.definition:
Improved: He has much furniture / many pieces of furniture.

Rule: Furniture is uncountable.

Memory hook: Furniture never becomes furnitures.

cards.term: Error: The sceneries of Kashmir are beautiful.
cards.definition:
Improved: The scenery of Kashmir is beautiful.

Rule: Scenery is uncountable.

Memory hook: Scenery is a whole view, not countable pieces.

cards.term: Error: He gave me informations.
cards.definition:
Improved: He gave me information.

Rule: Information is uncountable.

Memory hook: Information does not take plural s.

cards.term: Error: He has done a great progress.
cards.definition:
Improved: He has made great progress.

Rule: Use make progress, not do progress.

Memory hook: Progress is made, not done.

cards.term: Error: She did a mistake.
cards.definition:
Improved: She made a mistake.

Rule: Use make a mistake.

Memory hook: Mistakes are made, sadly very easily.

cards.term: Error: He gave an exam yesterday.
cards.definition:
Improved: He took an exam yesterday.

Rule: Students take exams, teachers give exams.

Memory hook: Examiners give, candidates take.

cards.term: Error: He passed out from college in 2020.
cards.definition:
Improved: He graduated from college in 2020.

Rule: Pass out can mean faint in standard English, use graduated for completing college.

Memory hook: In exams, pass out is risky Indian English.

cards.term: Error: He is giving exam next week.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is taking an exam next week.

Rule: A candidate takes an exam.

Memory hook: Do not let Indian English steal the mark.

cards.term: Error: She is doing a job in a bank.
cards.definition:
Improved: She works in a bank.

Rule: Work in a bank is cleaner standard English.

Memory hook: Do a job is often awkward.

cards.term: Error: He is sitting on the computer.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is working at the computer.

Rule: Use at the computer for working, on may sound physically on top.

Memory hook: Unless he is literally on the CPU, use at.

cards.term: Error: Please off the light.
cards.definition:
Improved: Please switch off the light.

Rule: Use switch off, not off as a verb in formal English.

Memory hook: Off is not the full verb here.

cards.term: Error: Please on the fan.
cards.definition:
Improved: Please switch on the fan.

Rule: Use switch on.

Memory hook: Fans need switch on, not simply on.

cards.term: Error: I will discuss with you about the plan.
cards.definition:
Improved: I will discuss the plan with you.

Rule: Discuss takes object directly, and with for person.

Memory hook: Discuss the matter with someone.

cards.term: Error: He is in the habit to smoke.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is in the habit of smoking.

Rule: In the habit of takes gerund.

Memory hook: Habit of doing.

cards.term: Error: She is under the impression that he is honest.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is under the impression that he is honest.

Rule: This phrase is correct.

Memory hook: Under the impression is a valid idiom.

cards.term: Error: He is under wrong impression.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is under the wrong impression.

Rule: Use the with specific impression.

Memory hook: Impression becomes specific here.

cards.term: Error: He caught me by my hand.
cards.definition:
Improved: He caught me by the hand.

Rule: Use by the body part in this idiom.

Memory hook: Caught by the hand, not by my hand.

cards.term: Error: She looked me in my face.
cards.definition:
Improved: She looked me in the face.

Rule: Use the with body part in such idioms.

Memory hook: Body-part idioms often use the.

cards.term: Error: He hit me on my head.
cards.definition:
Improved: He hit me on the head.

Rule: Use the with body part after hit in such expressions.

Memory hook: The head is idiomatic here.

cards.term: Error: He has a good command on English.
cards.definition:
Improved: He has a good command of English.

Rule: Command of a language.

Memory hook: Language command uses of.

cards.term: Error: He is expert in English.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is an expert in English.

Rule: Expert as noun needs an article.

Memory hook: An expert is a person, expert alone is adjective.

cards.term: Error: She is expert at solving puzzles.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is expert at solving puzzles.

Rule: This is correct when expert is adjective.

Memory hook: Expert can be adjective without article.

cards.term: Error: He has no control on his anger.
cards.definition:
Improved: He has no control over his anger.

Rule: Control over something.

Memory hook: Control sits over.

cards.term: Error: She has influence on him.
cards.definition:
Improved: She has influence over him.

Rule: Influence over a person is standard.

Memory hook: Influence controls from over.

cards.term: Error: This has no effect on me.
cards.definition:
Improved: This has no effect on me.

Rule: Effect on is correct.

Memory hook: Effect lands on the affected thing.

cards.term: Error: He has an access to the library.
cards.definition:
Improved: He has access to the library.

Rule: Access is usually uncountable in this sense.

Memory hook: Access does not need an here.

cards.term: Error: He has a great knowledge of history.
cards.definition:
Improved: He has great knowledge of history.

Rule: Knowledge is usually uncountable.

Memory hook: Knowledge stands without a.

cards.term: Error: Please advice me.
cards.definition:
Improved: Please advise me.

Rule: Advise is the verb, advice is the noun.

Memory hook: You give advice, you advise someone.

cards.term: Error: His advise was useful.
cards.definition:
Improved: His advice was useful.

Rule: Advice is the noun.

Memory hook: The noun has c.

cards.term: Error: This will effect your marks.
cards.definition:
Improved: This will affect your marks.

Rule: Affect is usually the verb meaning influence.

Memory hook: Affect acts, effect results.

cards.term: Error: The affect of pollution is visible.
cards.definition:
Improved: The effect of pollution is visible.

Rule: Effect is the noun meaning result.

Memory hook: Effect is the result.

cards.term: Error: He excepted my proposal.
cards.definition:
Improved: He accepted my proposal.

Rule: Accept means agree or receive.

Memory hook: Except excludes, accept receives.

cards.term: Error: Everyone came accept Ravi.
cards.definition:
Improved: Everyone came except Ravi.

Rule: Except means excluding.

Memory hook: Except throws Ravi out of the group.

cards.term: Error: The principal of honesty is important.
cards.definition:
Improved: The principle of honesty is important.

Rule: Principle means rule or belief.

Memory hook: A rule ends with le.

cards.term: Error: The principle called a meeting.
cards.definition:
Improved: The principal called a meeting.

Rule: Principal means head of a school or main.

Memory hook: School head is principal.

cards.term: Error: She lost her stationary.
cards.definition:
Improved: She lost her stationery.

Rule: Stationery means writing materials.

Memory hook: Paper has e, stationery has e.

cards.term: Error: The bus was stationery.
cards.definition:
Improved: The bus was stationary.

Rule: Stationary means not moving.

Memory hook: Stationary has a for at rest.

cards.term: Error: He is very week.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is very weak.

Rule: Weak means not strong.

Memory hook: Week is seven days.

cards.term: Error: I will come next weak.
cards.definition:
Improved: I will come next week.

Rule: Week means seven days.

Memory hook: A week is time, weak is strength.

cards.term: Error: The site was beautiful to see.
cards.definition:
Improved: The sight was beautiful to see.

Rule: Sight means view.

Memory hook: Sight is what you see.

cards.term: Error: The construction sight is closed.
cards.definition:
Improved: The construction site is closed.

Rule: Site means place.

Memory hook: Site is location.

cards.term: Error: He cited at the beautiful view.
cards.definition:
Improved: He looked at the beautiful view.

Rule: Cite means quote, not see.

Memory hook: Cite belongs to references.

cards.term: Error: She has a sweet voice and good moral.
cards.definition:
Improved: She has a sweet voice and good morale.

Rule: Morale means confidence or spirit.

Memory hook: Team spirit is morale.

cards.term: Error: The moral of the team is high.
cards.definition:
Improved: The morale of the team is high.

Rule: Morale means group confidence.

Memory hook: Moral is lesson or ethics.

cards.term: Error: He gave me complement.
cards.definition:
Improved: He gave me a compliment.

Rule: Compliment means praise.

Memory hook: Praise has i inside compliment.

cards.term: Error: This scarf compliments the dress.
cards.definition:
Improved: This scarf complements the dress.

Rule: Complement means completes or goes well with.

Memory hook: Complement completes.

cards.term: Error: The story is not creditable.
cards.definition:
Improved: The story is not credible.

Rule: Credible means believable.

Memory hook: Credible is about belief.

cards.term: Error: His performance was credible.
cards.definition:
Improved: His performance was creditable.

Rule: Creditable means deserving praise.

Memory hook: Creditable earns credit.

cards.term: Error: The medicine is very affective.
cards.definition:
Improved: The medicine is very effective.

Rule: Effective means producing result.

Memory hook: Effective has effect inside it.

cards.term: Error: He is an eminent danger.
cards.definition:
