Improved: He is in imminent danger.

Rule: Imminent means about to happen.

Memory hook: Imminent means incoming.

cards.term: Error: An imminent scholar visited us.
cards.definition:
Improved: An eminent scholar visited us.

Rule: Eminent means famous and respected.

Memory hook: Eminent means elevated in reputation.

cards.term: Error: The teacher eluded to a poem.
cards.definition:
Improved: The teacher alluded to a poem.

Rule: Allude means refer indirectly.

Memory hook: Allude points softly.

cards.term: Error: The thief alluded the police.
cards.definition:
Improved: The thief eluded the police.

Rule: Elude means escape.

Memory hook: Elude escapes.

cards.term: Error: The data is not illegible for the post.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is not eligible for the post.

Rule: Eligible means qualified.

Memory hook: Eligible can enter.

cards.term: Error: His handwriting is eligible.
cards.definition:
Improved: His handwriting is legible.

Rule: Legible means readable.

Memory hook: Legible letters can be read.

cards.term: Error: This is an illicit response.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is an elicited response.

Rule: Elicit means draw out a response.

Memory hook: Elicit extracts an answer.

cards.term: Error: They ran an elicit business.
cards.definition:
Improved: They ran an illicit business.

Rule: Illicit means illegal.

Memory hook: Illicit is illegal.

cards.term: Error: He adopted to the new city quickly.
cards.definition:
Improved: He adapted to the new city quickly.

Rule: Adapt means adjust.

Memory hook: Adapt adjusts.

cards.term: Error: They adapted a child.
cards.definition:
Improved: They adopted a child.

Rule: Adopt means take as one's own.

Memory hook: Adopt brings into family.

cards.term: Error: He said me that he was busy.
cards.definition:
Improved: He told me that he was busy.

Rule: Tell takes an object, say does not work this way.

Memory hook: Said me is a common trap.

cards.term: Error: She told that she was ill.
cards.definition:
Improved: She said that she was ill.

Rule: Tell needs a personal object.

Memory hook: Tell someone, say something.

cards.term: Error: He asked me where do I live.
cards.definition:
Improved: He asked me where I lived.

Rule: Indirect questions use statement order.

Memory hook: No do/does question order inside indirect speech.

cards.term: Error: She asked why was I late.
cards.definition:
Improved: She asked why I was late.

Rule: Indirect questions use statement word order.

Memory hook: Question becomes a statement after asked.

cards.term: Error: He asked me did I finish it.
cards.definition:
Improved: He asked me whether I had finished it.

Rule: Yes/no indirect questions use whether/if.

Memory hook: Did disappears into whether.

cards.term: Error: He said that he will come.
cards.definition:
Improved: He said that he would come.

Rule: After past reporting verb, will changes to would.

Memory hook: Said pulls will back to would.

cards.term: Error: She said that she is tired.
cards.definition:
Improved: She said that she was tired.

Rule: Present tense usually backshifts after past reporting verb.

Memory hook: Said makes is become was.

cards.term: Error: The teacher said that the earth moved around the sun.
cards.definition:
Improved: The teacher said that the earth moves around the sun.

Rule: Universal truths do not backshift.

Memory hook: Science does not obey reported-speech panic.

cards.term: Error: He said, that he was ready.
cards.definition:
Improved: He said that he was ready.

Rule: Do not put a comma before that in indirect speech.

Memory hook: Direct speech uses comma before quote, indirect usually does not.

cards.term: Error: She requested me that I should help her.
cards.definition:
Improved: She requested me to help her.

Rule: Request takes object plus to-infinitive.

Memory hook: Please becomes requested to.

cards.term: Error: He ordered me that I should leave.
cards.definition:
Improved: He ordered me to leave.

Rule: Order takes object plus to-infinitive.

Memory hook: Command becomes to leave.

cards.term: Error: The teacher advised to me to revise.
cards.definition:
Improved: The teacher advised me to revise.

Rule: Advise takes direct object, no to before me.

Memory hook: Advise someone to do.

cards.term: Error: He suggested me to apply.
cards.definition:
Improved: He suggested that I apply.

Rule: Suggest does not normally take object plus to-infinitive.

Memory hook: Suggest that is the exam-safe structure.

cards.term: Error: The letter was wrote by him.
cards.definition:
Improved: The letter was written by him.

Rule: Passive voice uses be plus V3.

Memory hook: Was wrote is not passive, was written is.

cards.term: Error: English is speak here.
cards.definition:
Improved: English is spoken here.

Rule: Passive uses is/am/are plus V3.

Memory hook: Language is spoken, not speak.

cards.term: Error: The road is repairing.
cards.definition:
Improved: The road is being repaired.

Rule: Passive continuous uses is being plus V3.

Memory hook: Roads do not repair themselves in this meaning.

cards.term: Error: The thief has arrested.
cards.definition:
Improved: The thief has been arrested.

Rule: Perfect passive uses has been plus V3.

Memory hook: If police did it, use been.

cards.term: Error: The work will finish tomorrow.
cards.definition:
Improved: The work will be finished tomorrow.

Rule: Future passive uses will be plus V3.

Memory hook: Work is not finishing itself here.

cards.term: Error: He was died in 2010.
cards.definition:
Improved: He died in 2010.

Rule: Die is intransitive and not passive.

Memory hook: Nobody is died in standard grammar.

cards.term: Error: The accident was happened yesterday.
cards.definition:
Improved: The accident happened yesterday.

Rule: Happen is intransitive and not passive.

Memory hook: Was happened is a classic error.

cards.term: Error: The meeting was occurred at noon.
cards.definition:
Improved: The meeting occurred at noon.

Rule: Occur is intransitive.

Memory hook: Events occur, they are not occurred.

cards.term: Error: The sun was risen.
cards.definition:
Improved: The sun rose.

Rule: Rise is intransitive and not passive.

Memory hook: The sun rises by itself.

cards.term: Error: The matter was discussed about.
cards.definition:
Improved: The matter was discussed.

Rule: Discuss takes direct object, no about.

Memory hook: Discuss already includes about.

cards.term: Error: The rules must followed.
cards.definition:
Improved: The rules must be followed.

Rule: Modal passive requires be plus V3.

Memory hook: Must be followed is the full passive.

cards.term: Error: This question can solved easily.
cards.definition:
Improved: This question can be solved easily.

Rule: Modal passive uses can be plus V3.

Memory hook: Can needs be before solved.

cards.term: Error: Let the door opened.
cards.definition:
Improved: Let the door be opened.

Rule: Imperative passive uses let + object + be + V3.

Memory hook: Let passive needs be.

cards.term: Error: The book has been wrote.
cards.definition:
Improved: The book has been written.

Rule: Perfect passive requires V3 written.

Memory hook: Been does not rescue a wrong verb form.

cards.term: Error: He was gave a prize.
cards.definition:
Improved: He was given a prize.

Rule: Passive of give is was given.

Memory hook: Prize comes with given.

cards.term: Error: The match was won by India yesterday.
cards.definition:
Improved: The match was won by India yesterday.

Rule: This sentence is correct.

Memory hook: Passive with was won is valid.

cards.term: Error: The homework has done by me.
cards.definition:
Improved: The homework has been done by me.

Rule: Perfect passive needs has been done.

Memory hook: Homework cannot has done by itself.

cards.term: Error: I am having two brothers.
cards.definition:
Improved: I have two brothers.

Rule: Have meaning possession is not normally continuous.

Memory hook: Family members are possessed with have, not having.

cards.term: Error: He is knowing the truth.
cards.definition:
Improved: He knows the truth.

Rule: Know is a stative verb.

Memory hook: Truth is known, not knowing.

cards.term: Error: She is resembling her mother.
cards.definition:
Improved: She resembles her mother.

Rule: Resemble is stative and not normally continuous.

Memory hook: Faces resemble, they do not resemble-ing.

cards.term: Error: This curry is tasting good.
cards.definition:
Improved: This curry tastes good.

Rule: Taste as quality takes simple present.

Memory hook: Food tastes good.

cards.term: Error: The rose is smelling sweet.
cards.definition:
Improved: The rose smells sweet.

Rule: Smell as quality takes simple present.

Memory hook: Flowers smell, noses smell them.

cards.term: Error: I am believing you.
cards.definition:
Improved: I believe you.

Rule: Believe is stative.

Memory hook: Belief prefers simple present.

cards.term: Error: He is wanting a new phone.
cards.definition:
Improved: He wants a new phone.

Rule: Want is stative.

Memory hook: Desire does not need continuous.

cards.term: Error: This pen is belonging to me.
cards.definition:
Improved: This pen belongs to me.

Rule: Belong is stative.

Memory hook: Belong refuses -ing.

cards.term: Error: She is understanding the lesson.
cards.definition:
Improved: She understands the lesson.

Rule: Understand is stative.

Memory hook: Understanding becomes understands.

cards.term: Error: He is seeing the mistake now.
cards.definition:
Improved: He sees the mistake now.

Rule: See meaning understand is stative.

Memory hook: Realisation uses sees.

cards.term: Error: I have headache.
cards.definition:
Improved: I have a headache.

Rule: Use an article before singular countable headache.

Memory hook: Headache is countable here.

cards.term: Error: She has fever.
cards.definition:
Improved: She has a fever.

Rule: Use a fever in standard countable use.

Memory hook: A fever is one unpleasant guest.

cards.term: Error: He is suffering from a fever.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is suffering from fever / He has a fever.

Rule: Both can be acceptable, but avoid awkward overuse.

Memory hook: Choose a natural phrasing.

cards.term: Error: I am going to my home.
cards.definition:
Improved: I am going home.

Rule: Go home usually takes no to/my in this simple phrase.

Memory hook: Home behaves like an adverb here.

cards.term: Error: He reached at the station late.
cards.definition:
Improved: He reached the station late.

Rule: Reach takes direct object.

Memory hook: Reach does not need at.

cards.term: Error: She discussed about the matter with me.
cards.definition:
Improved: She discussed the matter with me.

Rule: Discuss takes direct object.

Memory hook: Discuss the matter, not discuss about.

cards.term: Error: He emphasized on discipline.
cards.definition:
Improved: He emphasized discipline.

Rule: Emphasize takes direct object.

Memory hook: Emphasize already means put stress on.

cards.term: Error: He stressed on the need for reform.
cards.definition:
Improved: He stressed the need for reform.

Rule: Stress as verb takes direct object.

Memory hook: Stress the need, not stress on.

cards.term: Error: He ordered me to immediately leave.
cards.definition:
Improved: He ordered me to leave immediately.

Rule: Avoid split infinitive in formal exam correction when a cleaner option exists.

Memory hook: Put immediately after leave.

cards.term: Error: He asked for my permission to leave.
cards.definition:
Improved: He asked my permission to leave.

Rule: Both forms occur, but asked for permission is also acceptable.

Memory hook: Be careful: not every phrase is an error.

cards.term: Error: I doubt that he will not come.
cards.definition:
Improved: I doubt that he will come.

Rule: Doubt already implies uncertainty/negative expectation in this structure.

Memory hook: Do not add extra negative unless intended.

cards.term: Error: I do not doubt but that he will win.
cards.definition:
Improved: I do not doubt that he will win.

Rule: Avoid the archaic but that in modern standard English.

Memory hook: Keep the clause clean.

cards.term: Error: He is not only a teacher but also a poet.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is not only a teacher but also a poet.

Rule: This is correct.

Memory hook: Balanced noun phrase on both sides.

cards.term: Error: He is one of those who works hard.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is one of those who work hard.

Rule: Who refers to those, so use plural verb work.

Memory hook: Those work, one is selected from them.

cards.term: Error: This is the only one of those books that are useful.
cards.definition:
Improved: This is the only one of those books that is useful.

Rule: Only one makes the antecedent singular.

Memory hook: Only one is the subject of is useful.

cards.term: Error: He has no money to buy food.
cards.definition:
Improved: He has no money with which to buy food / He has no money to buy food.

Rule: The original is acceptable in modern usage.

Memory hook: Avoid overcorrecting natural English.

cards.term: Error: Scarcely had I entered the room when the phone rang.
cards.definition:
Improved: Scarcely had I entered the room when the phone rang.

Rule: This is correct.

Memory hook: Scarcely pairs with when.

cards.term: Error: No sooner had I reached than it began to rain.
cards.definition:
Improved: No sooner had I reached than it began to rain.

Rule: This is correct.

Memory hook: No sooner pairs with than.

cards.term: Error: He is too honest that he cannot cheat.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is too honest to cheat.

Rule: Too takes to-infinitive.

Memory hook: Too honest to cheat is compact.

cards.term: Error: He is so honest to cheat.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is so honest that he cannot cheat.

Rule: So takes that-clause.

Memory hook: So honest that he cannot cheat.

cards.term: Error: She is such honest that everyone trusts her.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is so honest that everyone trusts her.

Rule: Use so with adjective alone.

Memory hook: Such needs a noun phrase.

cards.term: Error: She is such an honest woman that everyone trusts her.
cards.definition:
Improved: She is such an honest woman that everyone trusts her.

Rule: This is correct.

Memory hook: Such + article + adjective + noun.

cards.term: Error: He is a man of words.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is a man of his word.

Rule: A man of his word means a reliable person.

Memory hook: One missing his changes the idiom.

cards.term: Error: He takes pain to help others.
cards.definition:
Improved: He takes pains to help others.

Rule: Take pains means make great effort.

Memory hook: Pains is plural in this idiom.

cards.term: Error: She gave him a piece of her mind.
cards.definition:
Improved: She gave him a piece of her mind.

Rule: This is correct idiom meaning scolded him.

Memory hook: Not every strange phrase is wrong.

cards.term: Error: He did not pay heed to my advice.
cards.definition:
Improved: He did not pay heed to my advice.

Rule: This is correct.

Memory hook: Pay heed to means give attention.

cards.term: Error: He paid no attention on the warning.
cards.definition:
Improved: He paid no attention to the warning.

Rule: Attention takes to.

Memory hook: Attention points to something.

cards.term: Error: He is in the good books of his teacher.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is in the good books of his teacher.

Rule: This is correct idiom.

Memory hook: Good books means favoured.

cards.term: Error: He is in good book of his teacher.
cards.definition:
Improved: He is in the good books of his teacher.

Rule: Correct idiom is in the good books of.

Memory hook: Both the and plural books matter.
